body: The --help verb group rows (contract/cli-verbs/help, contract/viola-help/verb-groups) are stale. Their setup row lists open, run, revive, verify, plugin install, but the built row is open, run, revive, up, verify, plugin install.

contract/viola-revive/no-window: a revive now places a window only under the hidden --origin flag. It moves to the workspace a real snapshot recorded, or reads unplaced. Without the flag there is no window step.

The revive usage and verb rows (contract/cli-verbs/revive, contract/viola-revive/usage, contract/viola-verb-help/usage) gain a hidden --origin <cli|agent>. It takes closed values, conflicts with --list, and has no --place.
contract/viola-revive/preflight-order: preflight now derives the window ask from --origin and the recovered snapshot.

The exit-code rows, through the new verb: contract/cli-exit-codes/21 now also covers up's board strict refusal (instance-unreachable or strict-modes-failed). up's exit 1 carries the refusal documents boot-time-unread, strict-modes-failed, pinned-hash-mismatch and terminal-not-found (contract/cli-exit-codes/json-form, contract/instance-unreachable-detail/strict-modes-failed).

The hint conventions (decision/hint-for-every-cause, decision/hint-last-on-stderr, decision/hints-name-next-verb, decision/hints-never-quote-or-locate) now rule over a new refusal word, boot-time-unread, with its own hint pair, and over up's single not-live hint line on stderr.

The refusal line form and the shared refusal word column (contract/cli-refusal-line/form, decision/shared-refusal-word-column) now rule over up's refusals. contract/run-revive-start-json/pinned-hash-mismatch now has a second verb, up, that writes the same code.
The revive --json error words (contract/viola-revive-json/already-live, stale-heartbeat, no-session, cwd-missing, session-live) are reused as up's per-instance outcome words.
decision/json-on-every-data-verb and contract/cli-json-mode/one-document: up has a --json that gives one document, {"v":1,"ok":{"instances":[{"name","outcome","placement"}]}}.
decision/cli-holds-every-action and the MCP verb decisions (decision/mcp-hides-wheel-and-handoff-verbs, the contract/mcp-tools rows): up is a CLI-only verb with no MCP tool and no channel method.
decision/targets-are-wrapped-names and decision/flat-verbs: up takes optional names, each parsed as a ViolaName. Given names narrow the fleet, and a name that is not scanned reads not-taken.

The plain output rules (decision/plain-output-modes, decision/stdout-results-stderr-rest, decision/cli-field-separators, decision/human-output-is-contract, decision/no-spinner, decision/single-progress-pattern, decision/words-carry-every-state) now rule over up's lines. Each line is plain ASCII with no SGR and one write per line, on stdout, in the form <name>  <word> or <name>  live  <placement>.
decision/board-ordered-by-name has a near exception in up's line order: every line that is not a spawn comes first, in name order, then the spawned or would-open lines in spawn order (parents first).

The viola open rows (contract/cli-verbs/open, contract/viola-open/parent-default): open's terminal spawn and its live wait are now shared with up, and open's behaviour is unchanged. Open writes the terminal's process-start alone and no process-exit.
The name sheet: the command name up is now taken.

body_fields.fact: viola up [<NAME>...] [--dry-run] [--json] re-opens the fleet after a reboot. Each candidate instance is revived in its own terminal at its recorded working directory, parents before children, and instances already live are skipped. It is CLI-only, with no MCP tool and no channel method.

viola up prints one line per instance, <name>  <word> or <name>  live  <placement>, with the outcome words in a closed set: live, already-live, stale-heartbeat, would-open, no-session, cwd-missing, session-live, not-live, not-taken.

viola up exits 0 when every line reads live, already-live, stale-heartbeat or would-open, and 1 otherwise. It exits 21 for the board's strict refusal. It exits 1 with a document for boot-time-unread, strict-modes-failed, pinned-hash-mismatch and terminal-not-found.

viola up orders its lines with every non-spawn line first in name order, then the spawned or would-open lines in spawn order. With names given, the fleet narrows to them, and an unscanned name reads not-taken.
After its lines, viola up writes one stderr hint line when any line reads not-live, and none under --json. --dry-run prints the plan as would-open lines and spawns nothing.
viola up --json gives one document, {"v":1,"ok":{"instances":[{"name","outcome","placement"}]}}. No line and no document of up carries an address, a pid or a workspace.
boot-time-unread is a refusal word, exit 1, with its own human pair and hint. It is the refusal when the host's boot time cannot be read.

viola revive has a hidden --origin <cli|agent> that conflicts with --list and has no --place. Under it, the revived window moves to the workspace a real snapshot recorded, or reads unplaced when none was recorded.
The command name up is occupied by the viola up verb.

body:
Added the CLI verb viola up: after a reboot it reopens the fleet's pre-boot instances, parents first. Each gets a foot terminal running the pinned viola revive, live and stale ones are skipped, and it prints one line per instance.
viola up is CLI only (no MCP tool, no channel method). It scans the board strictly before any log opens, then logs to the caller's cli file only under a parsed VIOLA_NAME, with span cli.up. It writes one process-start subject terminal per spawned terminal and no process-exit for it, and no snapshot, event line or stamp.
Added a new exit-1 process-exit detail word, boot-time-unread, to the diag-line schema's process-exit detail enum and the exit-cause table. The exit-1 detail of viola up is not-live when any instance reads not-live, else none.
viola revive gains a hidden --origin cli|agent flag. Under it a revive moves its window to the workspace a real snapshot recorded, through the existing run.window span and window line. Without it there is no window step.
Measured: the obs rule and its master row that promise a process-start and process-exit pair around viola open's terminal are disproved. The code writes the process-start alone, and the rule is corrected to the code.
Test-only: one shared teardown for a stand-in terminal's process tree ends the truncated-coverage-profile red. An fd guard now re-reads the child's fd table until it settles within its 2 s deadline. A gated live-rig script (R4) is added, and the fake foot records each spawn.

body: contract/diag-subject/terminal is STALE: it promises a process-start and process-exit pair around the foot terminal viola open spawns. The code writes the process-start alone, viola up does the same, and the row must be set to say so.

contract/process-exit-detail/exit-1 gains the detail word boot-time-unread (exit 1, viola up when the host boot time cannot be read). The diag-line schema's process-exit detail enum grows by that one word.
decision/exit-1-detail-codes and decision/distinct-detail-code-per-exit-cause: a new exit-1 cause, boot-time-unread, takes its own distinct detail word and its own unable and hint pair.
decision/diag-schema-additive-only, decision/log-fields-additive-only and decision/log-schema-additive-only: the detail enum change is additive, one word, and must stay so.

The CLI process-log file rows (contract/cli-log-file/open, focus, revive-start, revive-list) and decision/cli-log-only-under-viola-name: a new verb, viola up, logs to the caller's cli file only under a parsed VIOLA_NAME.

The strict-modes refusal rows (decision/strict-modes-refusal-writes-no-line, decision/pre-open-strict-modes-refusal-silent, decision/strict-modes-failure-lines, contract/strict-modes-refusal-exit/1 and /21, contract/exit-21-detail/strict-modes-failed, contract/cli-json-error/strict-modes-failed): viola up refuses the strict board scan with exit 21 and no line, and a home-tree refusal after the scan with exit 1 strict-modes-failed.
contract/cli-exit-codes/21 and the exit-21 cause words: viola up joins the verbs exiting 21 on the board's strict refusal (instance-unreachable / strict-modes-failed).

The exit-1 detail rows for start causes (contract/exit-1-detail/no-session, cwd-missing, session-live, stale-heartbeat, already-live, pinned-hash-mismatch): viola up shows these as per-instance outcome words on its lines. Its own process-exit detail is not-live or none, and only its refusals write their own word (pinned-hash-mismatch, strict-modes-failed, terminal-not-found, boot-time-unread).

The state-recovered rows (contract/state-recovered/*, contract/state-recovered-detail/*) and decision/no-raw-snapshot-reads: viola up reads each instance through the replay reader and writes state-recovered as viola list does. It never calls the strict board read, so it writes no parse-rejected state-entry line.

Heartbeat liveness rows (decision/heartbeat-staleness-threshold, decision/heartbeat-liveness, contract/list-liveness/stale-threshold, decision/liveness-transitions-not-logged): viola up classifies liveness with the stale threshold on a real snapshot, and on a replayed one by the beat alone. A new beat-before-boot check reads the heartbeat mtime against the host boot time, and no line is written for it.
decision/no-endpoint-over-replayed-snapshot and decision/replayed-snapshot-unreachable: viola up takes a replayed snapshot's liveness from the heartbeat alone and never its endpoint.

contract/child-spawn-log/subject and contract/process-log/child-and-probe-lifecycle: the terminal subject now has a second spawner, viola up, through the shared terminal spawn. It writes a process-start per spawn and no process-exit.
Span rows (decision/cli-manual-dispatch-span, decision/static-span-names, decision/span-naming): a new manual dispatch span, cli.up.

Window placement rows (contract/run-span-attributes/run-window, contract/run-start-events/window-line, decision/window-line-untraced): a revive now places a window only under its hidden --origin flag, through the existing run.window span and window line.

Revive start rows (decision/revive-start-logs-as-run, decision/revive-preflight-order, contract/cli-log-file/revive-start): revive's preflight gains the window ask from --origin, which conflicts with --list. Revive start still logs as run.

Stream rows (contract/stdout-by-role/cli, decision/short-lived-verbs-stderr, contract/cli-stderr/refusal-pair): viola up writes one ASCII stdout line per instance, or one --json document, and one stderr hint line when any instance reads not-live (none under --json). Its refusals use fixed unable and hint pairs.

Path-free and lineage rows (decision/detail-codes-no-paths, decision/home-level-lines-path-free, decision/lineage-names-confined): viola up's lines and document carry codes and names only, with no address, pid or workspace. It reads the parent only to order the spawns.

decision/state-crate-sync-instrumentation and decision/uninstrumented-components: viola-state gains three readers that write no line and open no span: the boot-time read of /proc/stat, the beat-before-boot check and the ended-after-last-start read.
Agents-probe rows (decision/agents-cli-instrumented-at-boundary, contract/revive-process-log/agents-probe): viola up runs one claude agents read for its whole candidate set before ordering.
decision/no-sleep-based-log-waits: the new shared terminal teardown and the fd guard's settle wait poll within one deadline with yield_now between reads, not by sleeping.

decision/diag-lines-schema-checked-in-unit-tests and decision/schema-conformance-gate: the viola up cases schema-check every line they read, and the schema conformance check covers the new detail word.

body:
The session added the CLI verb viola up, which re-opens the fleet after a reboot. Its candidates are instances whose heartbeat predates the boot time, that are not live and whose session did not end after its last start. It opens them parents first, skips live ones, and writes one line per instance.
For each candidate, up spawns a foot terminal directly with a closed argv that starts the pinned viola revive <name> --origin <cli|agent> in the recorded cwd. It then waits for the instance to come up live under the bound open already uses.
viola revive gained a hidden --origin flag with two closed values. It conflicts with --list and replays the workspace that a real snapshot's window recorded. Without the flag there is no window step.
viola-state gained a boot-time reader that reads /proc/stat once under MAX_FRAME, a heartbeat-before-boot test, a bounded end-after-last-start events reader and a read accessor on the board scan. The diag schema's process-exit detail gained boot-time-unread.
Test-only work: one shared teardown for a stand-in terminal's process tree, a settle wait in the child-fd guard, the fake foot recording each spawn, and a new live R4 rig script that refuses R4b and a root inside a repository.
No dependency, config key, env var, MCP tool or channel method was added, and nothing was retired.

body_fields.fact: viola up is a CLI-only verb (no MCP tool, no channel method) whose outcome words are closed — live, already-live, stale-heartbeat, would-open, no-session, cwd-missing, session-live, not-live, not-taken — exit 0 only when every line is live, already-live, stale-heartbeat or would-open, else 1, and 21 on the board's strict refusal.
Named instances narrow viola up to them; a name not scanned reads not-taken, and with none it reads the whole fleet.

viola up selects an instance only when its heartbeat predates the boot and its log has no session-end after its last session-start; live and stale instances are skipped, and candidates spawn parents first, a missing parent a root, a cycle once.
boot-time-unread is an exit-1 cause of viola up with its own hint and process-exit detail word, witnessed by its unit pair only, since a host's boot-time source cannot be hidden from a case.
The boot time read and an instance log's end-after-last-start read are bounded readers.
viola revive places its window only under its hidden --origin, at the workspace a real snapshot recorded, else unplaced; without the flag a revive runs no window step.

A stand-in terminal's process tree is ended by one shared teardown: it kills first only a leaf whose recorded parent still runs, waits for every other member under one WITHIN deadline, and kills at the deadline only a pid whose start time still matches.
The child fd guard re-reads the child's fd table inside its existing 2 s deadline while a whole table holds a non-fixture home path, then asserts the last whole table unchanged.

The R4 live rig refuses its R4b phases first (r4b-not-granted) until granted, and its rehearse form reads windows from the instance's own window record and prints a reading that is not a live reading.
The fake foot stand-in records each spawn's pid and argv as one line of a spawn record beside itself, and still writes its argv file.
The name up is occupied as a viola CLI verb.
